item.title: Uniformising random greedy maximal independent sets on graphs with at most five vertices
item.description: arXiv:2611.26675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A random greedy algorithm scans the vertices of a finite graph in increasing order of independent exponential arrival times and accepts each vertex unless an accepted neighbour blocks it. We ask an inverse question: can strictly positive finite arrival rates be chosen so that the terminal inclusion-maximal independent sets are all equally likely? We call this exact property exponential greedy uniformisability (EGU). We establish the complete small-order classification: every finite simple graph on at most five vertices is EGU, with the unique exception of the five-vertex path $P_5$ up to graph isomorphism. A strict $2\times2$ probability minor provides an explicit obstruction for the exceptional graph; the positive cases are certified by graph-isomorphism reduction and exact constructive witnesses. We explain the independent-exponential-clock probability law and the formal Lean 4 verification, registered as Palomar PALOMAR-2026-11-19-000021 (version 1). The registration is a formal proof record, not a claim of novelty certification or journal peer review.
item.dc:creator: John Fairfax-Ball

item.title: Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics
item.description:
arXiv:2611.26930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.
item.dc:creator: Xuda Ye, Zhihan Zhang

item.title: Sparse Analytic Representation of Stationary Processes with Bounded Spectral Density
item.description: arXiv:2611.27152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider centered second-order stationary processes Y={Y_t}{t\in R} with bounded spectral density S_Y and develop a sparse analytic representation framework. A nontrivial stationary process on the real line generally does not belong to L^2(\Omega,L^2(R)), since stationarity implies E||Y||{L^2(R)}^2=\infty. To overcome this infinite-energy obstruction, we replace the sample-path viewpoint by the bounded linear operator \widetilde Y: L^2(R) \to L^2(\Omega), with \widetilde Y(f) = \int_{R} \hat{f}(\xi) Z_Y(d\xi), where Z_Y is the orthogonal random measure in the spectral representation of Y. Applying \widetilde Y to Cauchy kernels in the upper and lower half-planes yields random analytic functions U_+ and U_-. For \alpha>1, we prove U_+ \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^+)) and U_- \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^-)), where B_\alpha^2(C^\pm) are weighted Bergman spaces. We combine U_+ and U_- into U(\omega,z) = U_+ for z \in C^+, and U_- for z \in C^-, and with B_\alpha = B_\alpha^2(C^+) \oplus B_\alpha^2(C^-), prove U \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha). We establish boundary vanishing, energy identity, and convergence, and derive covariance identities for the coefficients. In L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha), we apply stochastic pre-orthogonal adaptive Fourier decomposition (SPOAFD) to U_+ and U_- separately, using normalized reproducing kernels of the Bergman spaces as dictionaries. The adaptive selection is determined by the spectral density. Finally, using the Poisson kernel and SPOAFD expansions, we establish weak mean-square convergence of the original process against test functions in C_c^\infty(R).
item.dc:creator: Yiqiao Zhang, Fang Yang, Tao Qian

item.title: The Number of Real Eigenvalues of a Random Sign Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.27245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R_n$ count the real eigenvalues of an $n\times n$ matrix with independent uniform $\pm1$ entries. We prove that $R_n/\sqrt n$ converges in $L^1$ to $\sqrt{2/\pi}$. In particular, $R_n=\Theta(\sqrt n)$ with probability tending to one, as conjectured by Vu.
item.dc:creator: Caden Young

item.title: Stochastic Differential Equations on the Simplex
item.description: arXiv:2611.27309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a framework for simplex-valued diffusion processes, formulated as solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by antisymmetric Brownian motion. Our edge-wise representation includes the multivariate Jacobi processes and the general class of continuous simplex-valued polynomial diffusions. Also, it allows bounded, locally Lipschitz state-dependent drift rates and edge weights. We establish weak solutions, as well as global strong existence and pathwise uniqueness for strictly positive initial states under a sufficient boundary non-attainment condition.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Guasoni, Eberhard Mayerhofer

item.title: Vanishing bond-percolation threshold implies vanishing contact-process threshold
item.description: arXiv:2611.27354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for any infinite, locally finite and connected graph $G$ and $p\in(0,1/2]$ the survival probability of the contact process with infection rate $\lambda\ge20p$ is at least $3/4$ times the bond percolation probability with retention probability $p$. In particular, $\lambda_c(G)\le20\,p_c(G)$ whenever $p_c(G)<1/2$, and $p_c(G)=0$ implies $\lambda_c(G)=0$. The proof uses a submartingale built from percolation clusters on finite balls. We contrast this with the SIR epidemic, in which every vertex is infected at most once, and for which there are graphs with $p_c(G)=0$ on which the SIR epidemic dies out almost surely for every infection rate.
item.dc:creator: Benedikt Jahnel, Lukas L\"uchtrath, Christian M\"onch

item.title: Energy-constrained Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.27594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For reflected Brownian motion in an interval of length $N$, we consider the first time at which the length of time since the most recent visit to the boundary reaches $M$; this random `lifetime' comes from the interpretation in which the Brownian motion has a finite energy capacity $M$, uses energy at unit rate in the interior, and gets its energy replenished up to $M$ on every visit to the boundary. We prove distributional asymptotics for the lifetime in three different regimes depending on the relative growth of $N$ and $M$; these one-dimensional results parallel results in the random walk case by Wade and Grinfeld. We also present some initial results on the multidimensional version of the problem, for one scaling regime in the case of a ball, and conjectures on the behaviour in general domains.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Randles, Andrew Wade

item.title: A Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations
item.description: arXiv:2611.27662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. We obtain existence and uniqueness results for arbitrary finite time horizons.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Keyworth

item.title: Large deviations and conditional laws for a time-integrated logarithm of averaged Gaussian squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.27682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systems with identical instantaneous power distributions can have very different probabilities of insufficient service over a fixed interval. We study the lower tail of the time-integrated logarithm of a weighted mean of $d$ independent squared Gaussian paths as $d\to\infty$. A global entropy inequality resolves the nonconvex service constraint, identifies the unique Gaussian minimizer and controls the nonlinear likelihood weight far from that minimizer. Combined with a joint local limit, it yields sharp probabilities at fixed internal thresholds and conditional path laws: a Fredholm determinant enters the leading factor, and tangential Gaussian fluctuations are independent of the exponential service deficit. The approximations extend through moderate deviations to the central scale. For stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck paths, cancellation in the radial likelihood expansion yields relative error $O(d^{-1})$ on compact positive parameter families with proportions and saddles separated from zero. Genuine temporal covariance attenuation by correlation kernels for a type of positive limiting proportion increases the lower-tail rate, yet the finite-sample outage distributions cross near typical service. Thus one-time power distributions alone do not determine reliability.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Xu, Huazhong Zhao

item.title: Solvers for a Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations
item.description: arXiv:2611.27748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. Under our assumptions we derive two solvers: a martingale solver (inspired by the deep FBSDE solver studied in recent literature), and a min-max solver leveraging a Hilbert space orthogonality condition to enforce the martingale property. We obtain a posteriori error bounds for both solvers. The min-max solver avoids the need to approximate the class of square integrable martingales directly (which in practice is usually done by parameterizing a stochastic integral representation), at the expense of weakening the topology with respect to which one should expect convergence of an approximate solution.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Keyworth

item.title: Brownian Twins of Fractional Diffusion Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.27802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study generative diffusion models in which the Brownian motion driving the noising dynamics is replaced by fractional Brownian motion or by a Markovian approximation of it. In the standard linear-Gaussian setting, we show that the memory of the noise acts only through the noise schedule. To every such model we associate a Brownian twin, a classical diffusion model with the same drift and an explicit variance schedule, and prove that everything the reverse-time process knows about the data is contained in one linear statistic which follows the reverse-time equation of the twin. Consequently, the denoising score matching losses of the two models coincide for every network, and access to the full path or to the augmented state does not reduce the loss. Moreover, we characterize when the reduction degenerates and describe where the reduction ends.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Knochenhauer

item.title: No roughening transition for the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 4$
item.description: arXiv:2611.27805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the Ising measure $\mu_{\Lambda_n,\beta}^{\text{Dob}}$ on $\Lambda_n:=([-n,n]^{d-1}\times[-n,n-1]) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ at inverse temperature $\beta$ with all plus boundary condition at heights $z \geq 0$ and all minus boundary condition at heights $z<0$. Let $\beta_c(d)$ be the critical inverse temperature. For every $d \geq 4$ and $\beta>\beta_c(d)$, we prove that $\mu_{\Lambda_n,\beta}^{\text{Dob}}(\sigma_0)$ has a positive lower bound independent of $n$. As a consequence, any Dobrushin state (i.e., a subsequential limit of $\mu_{\Lambda_n,\beta}^{\text{Dob}}$) is not translation invariant for those $(d,\beta)$, and thus there is no roughening transition when $d \geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Jianping Jiang, Sike Lang

item.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
item.description: arXiv:2611.27828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Jungtaek Oh, Nurzhan Sapargali

item.title: How communities help epidemics persist
item.description: arXiv:2611.27843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical studies show that communities such as households and workplaces strongly influence how an infection spreads and how long it persists in a population. To understand this effect, we study the contact process (SIS epidemic model) on random intersection graphs and their local weak limit. In the contact process, infected vertices recover with rate $1$ and transmit the infection to each of their neighbours with rate $\lambda$. The random intersection graph is defined on a finite population; each individual belongs to a random number of communities (captured by a membership distribution), and each community has a random size (captured by a community size distribution). Communities are all taken to be complete graphs. The local weak limit of the random intersection graph, called the branching community tree, has complete graphs arranged in a tree structure. Letting $M$ have the membership distribution and $K$ have the community size distribution, we prove that if either $\mathbb E[e^{cM}]=\infty$ for all $c > 0$ or $\mathbb E[e^{cK\log K}] = \infty$ for all $c > 0$, then for all $\lambda > 0$, the infection on the finite graph survives for exponentially long with high probability, and on the local limit graph, it survives forever with positive probability. On the other hand, if for some $c > 0$ both $\mathbb E[e^{cM}]<\infty$ and $\mathbb E[e^{K\log(cK)}]<\infty$ hold, then the process with small $\lambda$ dies out in the local limit graph. We compare these findings with known results on the behaviour of the contact process on a "community-free" random graph with similar degree distributions, to highlight the impact of communities.
item.dc:creator: J\'ulia Komj\'athy, Marco Seiler, Daniel Valesin

item.title: Exit-Pair Rigidity, Neutral Restart Laws, and Inverse Reconstruction in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.27853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an absorbed one-dimensional diffusion, we characterize two-point restart laws preserving the exit-side probability for every independent renewal clock. Spectral identities establish rigidity under spatial accumulation, while explicit nonsymmetric potentials admit neutral pairs. We distinguish midpoint Dirichlet isospectrality from Weyl reflection rigidity and prove a second-order high-energy asymptotic under local continuity, giving two necessary asymmetry conditions for neutral pairs. Two complete exit profiles at distinct reset rates identify diffusivity and drift; a finite birth-death analogue admits exact Jacobi criteria and reconstruction from four channel functions.
item.dc:creator: Tony Newton, Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: The $H^{2|2}$-model and the Anderson model with Cauchy potential: similarities and a conjectured relation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We highlight strange similarities between the Anderson model with Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,\lambda)$ and the $H^{2|2}$ supersymmetric sigma field with initial non local conductances proportional to $W_{x,y}=\lambda^2\left \vert \left (-\Delta-E+ i\lambda)\right)_{x,y}^{-1}\right\vert^2$ where $\Delta$ is the discrete Laplace operator. More precisely, looking at the Brownian interpolation of both, we show that they follow very similar equations. Motivated by that we investigate the different phases of the $H^{2|2}$-model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with conductances $rW$ for some $r>0$ and show that whatever $r>0$ the $H^{2|2}$-model displays localized and delocalized phases which are coherent with what is expected or proved for the Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,\lambda)$. Finally, we propose a conjecture that compares key quantities of the two models and would imply existence of delocalized regime for the Anderson model with Cauchy potential in dimension $d\ge 3$.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Sabot

item.title: Optimal High-Dimensional Martingale CLTs over Rectangles
item.description: arXiv:2611.27929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Gaussian approximation bounds over rectangles for high-dimensional martingale sums, with lower bounds showing optimality up to powers of $\log n$. The results cover bounded increments, conditional and marginal sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential tails, and uniform $q$th-moment bounds on the largest absolute coordinate for $2<q\le3$. The predictable quadratic variation $Q$ may be random; the comparison Gaussian has deterministic covariance $\Sigma=\mathbb{E}Q$. We assume $\Sigma_{jj}=1$ and $\max_j\sum_k|\Sigma_{jk}|^s\le M$ for fixed $s>0$ and $M\ge1$, allowing $\Sigma$ to be singular, and quantify the error due to $Q-\Sigma$. Conditional tail bounds yield the same dimension threshold as boundedness, whereas marginal tail bounds give smaller thresholds. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform convergence in all these classes; under the uniform moment assumption, the criterion holds for every fixed $q>2$. When $Q=I_d$, the bounded and marginal light-tail rates have no additional factors in $\log n$ if $\log(ed)\ge\{\log(en)\}^2$; the same holds for the finite-moment rates with $2<q\le3$ in every dimension, for all sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Yao Su, Xiuqi Sun

item.title: Ehrhard-Type inequalities for radial measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.27935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Ehrhard-type inequalities for convex sets under rotationally invariant probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge2$, described by a radial density profile $\varphi$. We give sufficient conditions on the profile that apply to Gaussian and multivariate Student measures, including the Cauchy measure, and to a family of mixtures of two Student measures. We also prove necessary conditions on the profile and its tails. Together, these conditions determine the exact parameter range for this mixture family and characterize the rotationally invariant stable measures satisfying the inequality.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Byczkowski, Jacek Ma\l{}ecki, Tomasz \.Zak

item.title: Differential Transmutations and First-Passage Expansions for Monomial Brownian Boundaries
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Hernandez-del-Valle

item.title: Error analysis for the numerical approximation of the quantile hedging problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.26673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyse numerical approximations of quantile hedging in complete linear markets with Markovian diffusion dynamics. The problem is formulated as stochastic control for an augmented state $(X,P)$, where the probability martingale $P$ is constrained to $[0,1]$ and controlled through an unbounded volatility coefficient. We combine control truncation with piecewise-constant policy time-stepping (PCPT), stopping controls continuously upon boundary hitting to preserve the state constraint. Using one-step dynamic programming principles and regularisation, we derive a generator inequality and explicit value-function error bounds. Under standard coefficient regularity and a Lipschitz payoff, optimising the truncation and regularisation parameters yields an error exponent arbitrarily close to $1/8$ from below, uniformly in the probability variable. For controls bounded from the outset, we obtain exponents arbitrarily close to $1/4$ from below, approaching the exponent established by Jakobsen, Picarelli and Reisinger without state constraints. We also implement a fully discrete scheme with neural-network controls. Grid-time projection onto $[0,1]$ introduces a martingale defect and a pricing bias. We quantify this bias in a toy problem and mitigate it using a state-dependent control bound. Experiments in Black--Scholes and Lipschitz local-volatility models illustrate the correction and the decrease in pricing errors under grid refinement.
item.dc:creator: Cyril B\'en\'ezet, Cyril Nefzaoui-Blanchard, Sergio Pulido

item.title: Isolation in Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26781v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study isolation in the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$. When $p=o(1)$ and $np\to\infty$, allowing an $F$-free graph on the undominated vertices gives the same first-order asymptotics for every fixed forest $F$ as the domination number $\gamma(G)$ in $G(n,p)$. For the ordinary isolation number $\iota(G)$ ($F$ is an edge) we prove two-point concentration when $p$ is bounded away from $1$ and $np^2/(\log n)^3\to\infty$. We also identify a transition in the gap $\gamma(G)-\iota(G)$ when $\log(1/p)=o(\log n)$. This gap tends to infinity in probability when $p$ is well below $(\log\log n/\log n)^2$ and is at most one with high probability when $p$ is well above this scale. Finally, for every fixed graph $F$, we show that the classical minimum degree bound for domination is asymptotically sharp for $F$-isolation, even for regular host graphs.
item.dc:creator: Laurentiu Ploscaru

item.title: A functional Breuer-Major theorem under finite variance, with application to the $R/S$ test for long memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.26793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Breuer-Major theorem (Breuer and Major, 1983) states that, for a function $G$ of Hermite rank $m$ such that $\mathbb{E}(G^{2}(X))<\infty$, and a stationary Gaussian sequence whose correlation function $r$ satisfies $\sum_{i}|r(i)|^{m}<\infty$, the finite dimensional distributions of the normalized partial sum process of $G(X_{i})$ converge to those of a Brownian motion. Whether the functional version of this result holds under these sole conditions has remained open for a long time, the tightness being known only under additional moment assumptions. In this paper we prove that the functional central limit theorem holds under finite variance only. More generally, we give a high order expansion of the partial sum process which covers both short and long-range dependence: the long-range dependent components converge to Hermite processes, while the remainder converges to a Brownian motion. As an application, we discuss the question of testing long-memory in observed data using the $R/S$ statistics. We derive the limiting distributions of the classical and modified $R/S$ statistics, prove the consistency of the test and propose a data-driven choice of the truncation parameter. A Monte Carlo study compares the performances of the classical and modified $R/S$ statistics for both short-memory and long-memory sequences.
item.dc:creator: Samir Ben Hariz

item.title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method for Uncertain Particle Systems with Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.26946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Wenyi Wang, Lei Li, Yiwen Lin

item.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
item.description: arXiv:2611.26990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.
item.dc:creator: Alan J. Aw

item.title: How many states does an exact relaxation model need? Sharp state complexity and geometric obstructions for reversible chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.27406v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many states does a reversible Markov model need to reproduce two prescribed relaxation modes exactly? We maximize the smaller of the two stationary coordinate variances over all finite reversible chains whose states lie in a given convex region and whose coordinates relax at rates $1$ and $\rho$. Detailed balance turns this into the equilibrium of a tension-only cable network whose loads depend on the stationary masses. For the moment curve of the Wright-Fisher diffusion no finite chain is optimal: maximizing sequences converge to a unique beta law, and the best deficit with $N$ states is of order $N^{-2}$. We find the exact leading constant for states on the curve and for states in its convex hull, together with the optimal cube-root density of states. The hull constant is the curve constant times $c/(1+c)$, $c=(\rho-2)/\rho$; at $\rho=5/2$ the hull needs $\sqrt{6}$ times fewer states, although the limiting law is the same. For $\rho>8/3$ any upward enlargement of the hull lowers the constant again. All lower bounds hold for arbitrary transition graphs. At every fixed number of states an optimizer exists. On a seven-gon the smallest optimal chain jumps from three to four states while the optimal value stays constant, and a family of polygons forces the state count to grow linearly with the number of sides. Monotone vector fields give exact upper certificates, which solve an asymmetric quadrilateral at all rates and 381 polygon-rate instances in exact arithmetic. We formulate a finite-realizability problem and a finite-dictionary conjecture for polygons, and derive state budgets and exclusion tests for finite kinetic models.
item.dc:creator: Murad Aznagulov

item.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.27493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_\sigma$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(\Omega, \mathcal F_0; L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.
item.dc:creator: Bikram Podder, Surendra Kumar

item.title: Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2611.27687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(\mu\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows. Based on a dissipativity condition, we establish the pullback random asymptotic compactness and the compact random pullback attractor \(\mathcal A_\mu\). Finally, we prove that the family of random pullback attractors \(\mathcal A_\mu\) is upper semicontinuous at \(\mu=0\) almost surely.
item.dc:creator: Shiqi Li, Jiawei He, Jianhua Huang

item.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.27767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges, evaluating these integrals by residues determines the discrete closed-channel spectrum and yields expansions that agree with the analytic bootstrap predictions of Downing--Jacobsen--Nivesvivat--Ribault--Saleur.
item.dc:creator: Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu

item.title: A sharp dimension barrier for uniform Gaussian approximations
item.dc:creator: Anders Bredahl Kock

item.title: $L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.
item.dc:creator: Norman El Fartass, Lampros Gavalakis, Ioannis Kontoyiannis

item.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2611.27914v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.
item.dc:creator: Aryan Gadhave, Asghar Ghorbanpour, Liam Hickey, Masoud Khalkhali, Allison Klingler, Nathan Pagliaroli, Andrew Parks

item.title: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
item.description: arXiv:2611.27948v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.
item.dc:creator: Dominik Pabst, Michael A. Klatt, Klaus Mecke

item.title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.27969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.
item.dc:creator: Franziska Weber

item.title: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
item.description: arXiv:2001.01467v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls. These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.
item.dc:creator: Romain Tessera, Matthew Tointon

item.title: Asymptotic expansions for normal deviations of random walks conditioned to stay positive
item.description: arXiv:2412.09145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a one-dimensional random walk $S_n$ having i.i.d. increments with zero mean and finite variance. We continue our study of asymptotic expansions for local probabilities $\mathbf P(S_n=x,\tau_0>n)$, which has been started in \cite{DTW23}. Obtained there expansions make sense in the zone $x=o(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\log^{1/2} n})$ only. In the present paper we derive an alternative expansion, which deals with $x$ of order $\sqrt{n}$.
item.dc:creator: Denis Denisov, Alexander Tarasov, Vitali Wachtel

item.title: Characterisation of Markov property on planar maps
item.description: arXiv:2505.05447v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit, in a self contained way, the Markov property on planar maps and decorated planar maps from three perspectives. First, we characterize the laws on these planar maps that satisfy both the Markov property and rerooting invariance, showing that they are Boltzmann-type maps. Second, we provide a comprehensive characterization of random submaps, that we call stopping maps, satisfying the Markov property, demonstrating that they are not restricted to those obtained through a peeling procedure. Third, we introduce decorated metric planar maps in which edges are replaced by copies of random length intervals $[0,w_e]$, and the decorations are given by continuous functions on the edges. We define a probability measure on them that is the analogue of the Boltzmann map and show that it satisfies the Markov property even for sets that halt exploration mid-edge.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Araya, Luis Fredes, Avelio Sep\'ulveda

item.title: Contractive kinetic Langevin samplers beyond global Lipschitz continuity
item.description: arXiv:2509.12031v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we examine the problem of sampling from log-concave distributions with (possibly) superlinear gradient growth under kinetic (underdamped) Langevin algorithms. Using a carefully tailored taming scheme, we propose two novel discretizations of the kinetic Langevin SDE, the tamed exponential euler scheme and tamed OBABO and we show that they are both contractive and satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality. Building on this, we establish a series of non-asymptotic bounds in $2$-Wasserstein and total variation distance between the law reached by each algorithm and the underlying target measure. In particular, we show that both algorithms can reach almost optimal $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-1})$ convergence rate in Wasserstein and Total Variation distances, and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\epsilon^{-\frac{1}{2}})$ under increased Hessian local regularity for the tamed OBABO scheme.
item.dc:creator: Iosif Lytras, Panayotis Mertikopoulos

item.title: Asymptotic formulas for products of Poisson distributions
item.description: arXiv:2603.08598v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behaviour of the product tail probability $ \mathbb{P}(\xi_1\cdots\xi_N \geqslant n), $ where $\{\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\}$ is a finite collection of independent Poisson random variables with positive parameters $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N$. We derive a refined Laplace-type asymptotic formula for the tail probability, based on Stirling's logarithmic approximation, a constrained saddle-point method, the Lambert function, and a careful evaluation of the constrained Gaussian prefactor. This yields an explicit approximation with an $O(\log n)$ remainder term in the exponent.
item.dc:creator: D\v{z}iugas Chvoinikov, Jonas \v{S}iaulys

item.title: Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion: Definition and Fundamental Properties
item.description: arXiv:2606.02003v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the $n$-th order multifractional stable motion ($n$-MFSM), a symmetric $\al$-stable process ($\al\in(1,2]$) whose Hurst parameter is a function $H(t)\in(n-1,n)$, obtained by a Taylor regularization of order $n\ge1$ of the kernel of the linear multifractional stable motion. It contains the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of Kawai as the special case of constant $H$, and, up to explicit deterministic factors, the linear multifractional stable motion ($n=1$) and the moving-average $n$-th order multifractional Brownian motion ($\al=2$). We prove existence, give the harmonizable representation in the Gaussian case, and show that, if $H$ is of class $\mathcal C^n$ near $t_0$, the rescaled $n$-th order increments at $t_0$ converge in finite-dimensional distributions to the $n$-th order increments of the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of index $H(t_0)$. We then study the dependence structure through the codifference. For $s>0$ fixed and $H(t)\to H_+$ with $(H(t)-H_+)\log t\to0$, we obtain the exact power rate of $\tau(X(s),X(t))-c_0(s)$ as $t\to\infty$ away from the boundaries of three explicit parameter regimes, where $c_0(s)=\|X(s)\|_\al^\al$ if $\al<2$ and $c_0=0$ if $\al=2$; the constants are explicit and of known sign when $n\ge2$ or $\al=2$, while for $n=1$ and $\al<2$ part of one regime yields only convergence or a modified constant. In particular this codifference does not tend to zero when $n\ge2$. For the $n$-th order increments with constant $H$, whose codifference asymptotics were obtained by Kawai, we give a self-contained proof with the sign of the leading constants and treat the boundary cases of the long-range dependence criterion $H\ge n-1/\al$; for a non-constant Hurst function this criterion is extended only to functions that are eventually constant.
item.dc:creator: Atef Lechiheb

item.title: On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2607.05418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the group randomness of 0-1 real sequences derived from a binary linear code through the spectral anlysis of a suitable normalization of the Gram matrix of a $p \times n$ random matrix whose rows are uniformly and independently drawn from those 0-1 real sequences, where $p/n \to y \in (0,1)$. We show that as $n \to \infty$, its empirical spectral distribution converges to the Marchenko-Pastur law at a rate at least of the order $n^{-1/4}$ with high probability as a consequence of eigenvalue interlacing with the $\pm 1$ sequence model studied in 2021 [14], and that its largest eigenvalue, after centering by $p+1+y$, converges to a Gaussian random variable with mean 0 and variance $4y$, provided that the dual distance of the code is at least 5. Furthermore, we show that when this is the only control parameter, the lower bound 5 is optimal in general by demonstrating that the binary Simplex codes and first-order Reed-Muller codes of dual distance 3 and 4 respectively do not possess either property.
item.dc:creator: Chin Hei Chan

item.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
item.description: arXiv:2607.05693v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\to\tau$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(\tau/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.
item.dc:creator: Joon Hyung Lee

item.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2611.01905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_{\theta} = \smash{[ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]}$, for every fixed $\theta > 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $\sigma - 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + \theta})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(\sigma + \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.17625v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.
item.dc:creator: Richard Duong, Janis Auffenberg, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Weak and Strong Moments of Log-Concave Measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.18867v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+2e$. This bound implies Lata{\l}a's conjecture on weak and strong moments.
item.dc:creator: Haozhou Zhang

item.title: Extinction conditions for a two-sex branching process with random mating and overlapping generations
item.description: arXiv:2611.25193v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a modification of the bisexual branching process with random mating and overlapping generations. Unlike the model of Molina and Mota (2024), our modification introduces probabilistic age-dependent survival that depends on the state of the population. Our modification preserves the general properties of the original process. We establish two sufficient conditions characterizing the subcritical and supercritical regimes of the process, i.e., extinction of the population with probability one and survival of the population with positive probability. The results are illustrated with numerical simulations of the process performed in Python.
item.dc:creator: Nikita V. Gordeev, Manuel Mota, Elena B. Yarovaya

item.title: Slow Mixing of Quantum Gibbs Samplers
item.description: arXiv:2411.04300v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Preparing thermal (Gibbs) states is a common task in physics and computer science. Recent algorithms mimic cooling via system-bath coupling, where the cost is determined by mixing time, akin to classical Metropolis-like algorithms. However, few methods exist to demonstrate slow mixing in quantum systems, unlike the well-established classical tools for systems like the Ising model and constraint satisfaction problems. We present a quantum generalization of these tools through a generic bottleneck lemma that implies slow mixing in quantum systems. This lemma focuses on quantum measures of distance, analogous to the classical Hamming distance but rooted in uniquely quantum principles and quantified either through Bohr spectrum jumps or operator locality. Using our bottleneck lemma, we establish unconditional lower bounds on the mixing times of Gibbs samplers for several families of Hamiltonians at low temperatures. For classical Hamiltonians with mixing time lower bounds $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[\Omega(n^\alpha)]$, we prove that quantum Gibbs samplers also have $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[\Omega(n^\alpha)]$. This applies to models like random $K$-SAT instances and spin glasses. For stabilizer Hamiltonians, we provide a concise proof of exponential lower bounds $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[\Omega(n)]$ on mixing times of good $n$-qubit stabilizer codes at low constant temperature. Finally, we consider constant-degree classical Hamiltonians and show how to lift classical slow mixing results in the presence of a transverse field using Poisson Feynman-Kac techniques. We show generic results for models with linear free energy barriers, and we demonstrate that our techniques extend to models with sublinear free energy barriers by proving $T_\mathrm{mix} = \exp[n^{1/2-o(1)}]$ for the ferromagnetic 2D transverse field Ising model.
item.dc:creator: David Gamarnik, Bobak T. Kiani, Alexander Zlokapa

item.title: Rapid Mixing of Glauber Dynamics for Monotone Systems via Entropic Independence
item.description: arXiv:2507.11031v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics on monotone systems. For monotone systems satisfying the entropic independence condition, we prove a new mixing time comparison result for Glauber dynamics. For concrete applications, we obtain mixing time bounds from specified extremal configurations: $\tilde{O}(n)$ for the random cluster model induced by the ferromagnetic Ising model with consistently biased external fields, and $\tilde{O}(n^2)$ for the bipartite hardcore model under the one-sided uniqueness condition, where $n$ is the number of variables in the corresponding models, improving the best known results in [Chen and Zhang, SODA'23] and [Chen, Liu, and Yin, FOCS'23], respectively. Our proof combines ideas from the stochastic dominance argument in the classical censoring inequality and the recently developed high-dimensional expanders. The key step in the proof is a novel comparison result between the Glauber dynamics and the field dynamics for monotone systems.
item.dc:creator: Weiming Feng, Minji Yang

item.title: Numerical Analysis of 2D Stochastic Navier--Stokes Equations with Transport Noise: Regularity and Spatial Semidiscretization
item.description: arXiv:2512.03483v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper establishes a strong convergence rate for the spatial finite element discretization of a two-dimensional stochastic Navier--Stokes system with transport noise and no-slip boundary conditions on a convex polygonal domain. The main challenge arises from the lack of spatial $D(A)$-regularity of the solutio (where $A$ is the Stokes operator), which prevents the direct applicability of standard error analysis techniques. Under a smallness assumption on the transport noise, for a MINI-element spatial semidiscretization, we establish a strong convergence rate of order $h^{\varrho} \log\big(1 + \frac{1}{h}\big)$, where $\varrho \in (0,1/2)$.
item.dc:creator: Binjie Li, Qin Zhou

item.title: Power-Law Spectrum of the Random Feature Model
item.description: arXiv:2603.14578v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scaling laws for neural networks, in which the loss decays as a power-law in the number of parameters, data, and compute, depend fundamentally on the spectral structure of the data covariance, with power-law eigenvalue decay appearing ubiquitously in vision and language tasks. A central question is whether this spectral structure is preserved or destroyed when data passes through the basic building block of a neural network: a random linear projection followed by a nonlinear activation. We study this question for the random feature model: given data $x \sim N(0,H )\in \mathbb{R}^v$ where $H$ has $\alpha$-power-law spectrum ($\lambda_j( H ) \asymp j^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha > 1$), a Gaussian sketch matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}^{v\times d}$, and an entrywise polynomial $f$ of degree $p$, we characterize the eigenvalues of the population random-feature covariance $\mathbb{E}_{ x }[\frac{1}{d}f(. W ^\top x )^{\otimes 2}]$. We prove matching upper and lower bounds: for all $1 \leq j \leq c_1 d \log^{-(p+1)}(d)$, the $j$-th eigenvalue is of order $\left(\log^{p-1}(j+1)/j\right)^{\alpha}$. For $ c_1 d \log^{-(p+1)}(d)\leq j\leq d$, the $j$-th eigenvalue is of order $j^{-\alpha}$ up to a polylog factor. That is, the power-law exponent $\alpha$ is inherited exactly from the input covariance, modified only by a logarithmic correction that depends on the degree $p$ of the activation. The proof combines a dyadic head-tail decomposition with Wick chaos expansions for higher-order monomials and random matrix concentration inequalities; a Gaussian integration-by-parts argument then extends the result from monomials to polynomials
item.dc:creator: Elliot Paquette, Ke Liang Xiao, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Stopping models closed under pgf composition, and the stability of randomly stopped model extensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.30106v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Statistical model transformations based on randomly stopped sums, maxima, and minima are widely used to extend statistical models by introducing an additional parameter. We characterize the finite-dimensional positive stopping models for which these randomly stopped sum and extreme transformations act as statistically stable (idempotent) model extensions. Stability requires the underlying stopping model to be closed under pgf composition. We prove that any finite-dimensional, connected, positive stopping model closed under pgf composition necessarily forms a family of random variables whose pgfs commute. Using the associated Koenigs function, we establish that these models form a statistical manifold admitting a global, one-dimensional parametrization $\theta = \Pr(N=1) \in (0, \theta_*]$, in which the probability mass at $i$ is a polynomial in $\theta$ of degree at most $i$. Within this class, we further establish a duality between those models containing the identity variable (the ones yielding statistically stable extensions) and the set of all probability distributions supported on the positive integers. By providing numerous examples of stopping models closed under pgf composition, we clarify the assertion that, under certain conditions, the only stopping model that is so is geometric.
item.dc:creator: Jordi Valero, Josep Ginebra

item.title: A Dynamical Theory of LoRA in Continual Learning
item.description: arXiv:2609.39367v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite the widespread use of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), little is known about its dynamics in continual learning and the mechanisms by which low-rank updates affect catastrophic forgetting. We provide an asymptotically exact dynamical characterization of LoRA in a solvable two-task teacher-student model. In the high-dimensional online-learning limit, we derive a closed system of ordinary differential equations for a finite set of macroscopic order parameters, yielding exact expressions for the generalization errors throughout both the initial Task 1 learning phase and the subsequent LoRA fine-tuning on Task 2. The theory quantitatively matches finite-dimensional simulations and exposes two characteristic effects of LoRA: when the first-task representation is not yet specialized, low-rank adaptation reduces interference with features learned on the first task, but its initialization slows adaptation to the second task. Building on this mechanistic picture, we analyze a state-dependent masking strategy that freezes hidden units carrying the strongest first-task representations and restricts adaptation to the complementary subspace. This structural partitioning markedly reduces forgetting, while preserving plasticity on the new task. Our framework further clarifies the role of adapter rank: transfer improves only up to the intrinsic dimensionality of the target task and saturates beyond it, while forgetting continues to grow with rank. These results provide a dynamical and geometric account of how low-rank adaptation organizes information across sequential tasks, and are qualitatively reproduced on sequential MNIST and CIFAR-100 using a shallow network and ResNet-18, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Th\'eo Marchetta, Filippo Alessandroni, Alessandro Breccia, Alessandro Ingrosso, Federica Gerace

item.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
item.description: arXiv:2610.33659v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/\beta$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $\beta=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.
item.dc:creator: Paul Bourgade, Pierre Le Doussal, Gregory Schehr

item.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
item.description: arXiv:2610.34048v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Hidekazu Yoshioka, Motoh Tsujimura, Ayumi Hashiguchi

item.title: Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator
item.description: arXiv:2610.36699v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Jiayu He, Chao Zheng

item.title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.24564v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).
item.dc:creator: Lenka Kopfov\'a, Matthew Kwan, Richard Montgomery, Kalina Petrova

item.title: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.25961v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(\mu)$, where the Gibbs measure $\mu$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(\mu)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincar\'e inequality in the velocity variable.
item.dc:creator: Lukang Sun
